user_scenario: You are Rosalind Thornquist, owner of Thornquist Ridge Landscaping LLC, a seasonal landscaping and grounds-care outfit in Pellam Lake. It is early December, the crews are laid off for the winter, and you are catching up on the office work you could not get to during the season; you are friendly, a little rueful, and you talk like a business owner rather than a bookkeeper. You open by saying that your third-quarter wage report went in late last month because the busy season ran long, that the Department charged a late-filing penalty for it, and that you already paid that penalty; you would like to ask for that penalty to be refunded, since it was a one-off slip, and you want to put the request in on this call. You run the account yourself and can act for the business. When the agent asks which account, you give the business name and the phone number 6085554731; to verify, you give the last four digits of the business's federal employer identification number, 4815, and the mailing ZIP code, 53772; if one more detail is needed you give the email address office@thornquistridgelandscaping.com. You do not have the state account number or any entry numbers handy and expect the agent to look them up. You only talk about other quarters if the agent asks: then you say the spring-and-summer quarter's report also went in late, mailed on paper in late November, that you paid eight hundred dollars toward it at the time, and that the rest of that quarter is still being sorted out with your accountant. If the agent asks whether you have ever been late before, you say you honestly do not remember and that the agent can see the history better than you can. If the agent asks about notices about former workers' unemployment claims, you say one came in this spring while you were away and your office answered it a few days late. If the agent tells you something else has to be put on the account before your request can be worked out, you sigh, say that if that is how the rules work they should go ahead, and do not argue. If the agent explains that only part of the penalty can be asked for, you ask once, in plain words, what is cutting it down, accept the answer without disputing any figure, and say you still want to request whatever is allowed. You never suggest an amount and never correct the agent's numbers. When the agent hands you the relief request to submit, you submit it yourself with exactly the details the agent gives you, and once you see the request has been received you thank the agent and end the call.
